items.title: Finite Nonsignalling Resources Suffice to Simulate Entangled Qubits
items.abstract: A longstanding question in Bell nonlocality is whether finite-alphabet nonsignalling resources can reproduce the continuum of measurement correlations of partially entangled qubits. Here we resolve this problem by showing that every fixed pure two-qubit state admits an exact simulation of all local projective-measurement statistics using shared randomness and finitely many Popescu-Rohrlich (PR) boxes, without communication or postselection. The boxes operate in parallel, with a worst-case bound independent of the measurement settings: at most $128\cot^4θ$ calls for the Schmidt state $\cosθ|00\rangle+\sinθ|11\rangle$, $0<θ<π/4$. The key is an exact finite-selection method that reduces input-dependent continuous sampling to a choice from a fixed-length shared random list, implemented through a finite PR-box network. The construction extends to arbitrary mixed two-qubit states and local binary-outcome POVMs. This reveals a fundamental separation between the continuity of quantum measurement correlations and the alphabet size of the resources needed to simulate them, shedding light on the resource-theoretic structure of Bell nonlocality.
items.why: Every pure two-qubit state's projective statistics are exactly simulated with finitely many PR boxes, at most 128·cot⁴θ calls.

eli5.plain: They prove that the infinitely many possible measurement correlations of an entangled qubit pair can be faked exactly with a finite number of idealised nonlocal boxes and shared randomness.
eli5.how: A finite-selection trick turns choosing from a continuous family of measurement settings into picking from a fixed random list, which a network of PR boxes can implement with no communication.
eli5.matters: It sharpens how much nonlocality an entangled qubit pair carries: continuous correlations do not need a continuous resource, which changes how one should count 'quantum' in a Bell experiment.
eli5.caveat: The bound blows up as the state approaches product (θ→0), and PR boxes are hypothetical; this is a resource statement, not a physical model.

items.title: What does quantum parameter estimation estimate? A no-go result for true quantity values
items.abstract: We examine the conditions under which quantum parameter estimation is compatible with the concept of a ``true'' quantity value: a unique value of the estimated quantity that exists prior to and independently of measurement. While quantum parameter estimation typically assumes that the quantity to be estimated is a parameter, we argue that this assumption can be lifted, opening the way to a more general formulation of estimation that may apply even in situations where the quantity to be estimated is no longer a parameter, but instead a quantum variable susceptible to quantum fluctuations. We identify three assumptions that characterize the way estimation is often presented in the quantum metrology literature, namely, as a procedure for inferring an unknown ``true value", which is assumed to be unique and to exist prior to and independently of measurement. Using our more general framework, we prove a no-go theorem showing that the preceding assumptions are jointly incompatible with two further assumptions: the completeness of the quantum state (no `hidden variables'), and the presence of entanglement between the probe systems and the system under measurement. We note that the presence of such entanglement is a generic prediction of standard quantum theory. Consequently, if one is not willing to accept hidden variables, nor willing to modify standard quantum theory by introducing a new physical mechanism that destroys entanglement at some scale or regime, then a realist account of estimation is ultimately impossible.
items.why: No-go theorem: a unique pre-existing 'true value' in quantum estimation is incompatible with complete states plus probe–system entanglement.

eli5.plain: They prove that quantum metrology cannot mean 'finding out a value that was already there' unless you accept hidden variables or new physics that stops entanglement.
eli5.how: They generalise estimation to quantities that fluctuate quantum-mechanically, list the assumptions behind 'true value' talk, and show these clash with state completeness and generic probe–system entanglement.
eli5.matters: It puts the measurement problem inside ordinary parameter estimation, the language used for every qubit-frequency or photon-number estimate; realism about measured values has a price.
eli5.caveat: The theorem hinges on how 'true value' is formalised; a reader who treats parameters as classical settings, not quantum variables, escapes it.

items.title: Trapped-ion-based quantum repeater node across a 17 km metropolitan fiber
items.abstract: Concatenation of quantum repeater nodes has been proposed as a means to distribute entanglement efficiently across future long-distance networks. Here, we demonstrate a trapped-ion repeater node that establishes photonic entanglement over a 17 km fiber traversing a city, moving beyond laboratory-only prototypes. The node comprises two atomic ions coupled to an optical cavity. First, a detailed characterization is performed of the long fiber channel and of ion-photon entanglement distributed across it. Next, a repeater-node protocol is implemented, achieving entanglement between a local photon and a remote photon with a Bell-state fidelity of $81.6^{+1.9}_{-1.4}\%$. These results demonstrate that trapped-ion repeater-node technology can operate over existing city-scale fiber infrastructure and represent a step toward distributed quantum repeater networks.
items.why: Two ions in one cavity act as a repeater node, linking photons across 17 km of city fiber at 81.6% Bell-state fidelity.

eli5.plain: They built one middle station of a quantum repeater from two trapped ions and used it to entangle photons sent over a real 17 km city fiber.
eli5.how: Each ion emits a photon entangled with it into a shared cavity; one photon travels the long fiber, and a joint operation on the two ions swaps the entanglement onto the two photons.
eli5.matters: This is the deployed-fiber version of the node-to-node state transfer microwave networks are chasing; its loss and fidelity budget is a benchmark for any transducer-based superconducting link.
eli5.caveat: One node, 81.6% fidelity and a low success rate; a useful repeater chain needs several nodes beating direct transmission, which this does not yet show.

items.title: High-fidelity entanglement of two spectrally-distinct solid state emitters
items.abstract: Solid state quantum emitters with electronic spin properties can be entangled using optical interferometric which-path erasure techniques that rely on identical frequencies and linewidths of the emitters. This promises a powerful, fast and scalable platform for quantum technologies. Using current protocols, a pair of emitters embedded in a waveguide interferometer can be deterministically prepared in a maximally entangled state. However, the amount of entanglement diminishes rapidly with increasing separation of the emission lines and variations in the linewidths of the emitters. Solid state emitters such as quantum dots are subject to intrinsic variations in the fabrication process. Therefore, manufacturing the required number of identical emitters on a chip is not scalable. In this Letter, we present a method that uses readily available pairs of entangled photons to entangle solid state emitters with large transition frequency separations and linewidth variations, circumventing the need to fabricate optically identical emitters. We demonstrate a concurrence of C = 0.95 for typical quantum dots using narrowband photon inputs.
items.why: Feeding entangled photon pairs into two mismatched quantum dots entangles them at concurrence 0.95 despite different frequencies and linewidths.

eli5.plain: They propose a way to entangle two solid-state emitters that do not emit the same colour, by giving each a photon from an entangled pair instead of erasing which-path information.
eli5.how: Each emitter absorbs one photon of a pre-entangled narrowband pair, so the entanglement is imported rather than created by interfering identical emissions; mismatch then matters far less.
eli5.matters: Superconducting qubits are never identical either; importing entanglement from a shaped two-mode source is a protocol that maps onto microwave nodes with frequency spread.
eli5.caveat: Simulation only, with narrowband entangled photons assumed available at the right frequencies; absorption efficiency and source brightness set the real rate.

items.title: Interacting quantum reference frames
items.abstract: We formulate quantum reference frames within the Dirac quantization of gauge theories, where physical states are obtained from a kinematical Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}_{\rm kin}$ by group averaging. We assume the gauge group $G$ is unimodular, and we define a quantum reference frame as a system of coherent states associated with a group $G_R$ of frame orientations acting on a tensor factor of $\mathcal{H}_{\rm kin}$. In direct analogy with the Faddeev-Popov procedure in path integrals, we show that the physical inner product can be written in terms of a choice of frame orientation with an appropriate operator measure, but that the physical Hilbert space is independent of this choice of frame. This yields a generalization of the Page-Wootters reduction map used to define conditional states and conditional probabilities of measurement outcomes given a frame orientation. These probabilities correspond to the expectation values of relational Dirac observables obtained from generalizations of previously considered relativization maps. Our main result is that the map that implements a change of frame is unitary, even when $G$ does not act as a tensor-product representation across a factorization of $\mathcal{H}_{\rm kin}$. The formalism therefore accommodates interactions between reference frames and the systems described relative to them. We apply this formalism to temporal frames, showing that a unitary Schrödinger equation emerges for an interacting clock and system, and that a previously reported time-nonlocal Schrödinger equation is recovered in an appropriate limit. With this, problems of non-unitarity are avoided by the use of the gauge-fixing measure in the physical inner product. We also discuss the case of interacting spatial frames, where the known correspondence between coherence in one frame and entanglement in another is shown to depend on the coupling.
items.why: Frame changes stay unitary even with interacting reference frames, recovering a unitary clock-system Schrödinger equation.

eli5.plain: They extend the theory of quantum reference frames so that the 'ruler' or 'clock' can interact with what it measures, and show switching viewpoints is still a reversible operation.
eli5.how: Physical states come from averaging over a gauge group; choosing a frame orientation is like gauge fixing in path integrals, and the resulting change-of-frame map is unitary.
eli5.matters: It addresses whether time measured by a physical, interacting clock gives sensible quantum dynamics, a question underlying relational readings of quantum mechanics.
eli5.caveat: Formal and restricted to unimodular gauge groups; no experiment is proposed, and the interacting examples are simple models.

items.title: Photon-Number Discrimination from Increasing Time-of-Arrival Separation in Wide Superconducting Microstrip Single-Photon Detectors
items.abstract: Measurements of photon-number-dependent time-of-arrival (TOA) distributions in wide NbN superconducting microstrip single-photon detectors (SMSPDs) are presented. Two \SI{10}{\um}-long devices with widths of \SI{3.2}{\um} and \SI{6.4}{\um} are characterized under pulsed \SI{515}{nm} excitation. The TOA histograms are described by sums of exponentially modified Gaussian (EMG) components, with the wider device exhibiting components assigned to photon numbers up to \(n=8\). Adjacent TOA peaks become more distinguishable relative to their widths at higher photon number, in contrast to the compression of neighboring photon-number timing shifts observed in conventional narrow-wire SNSPDs. For the components assigned to \(n=7\) and \(n=8\), the FWHM-normalized peak separation is \(2.15\), and the fitted EMG distributions yield an equal-prior pairwise TOA-assignment fidelity of \(99.6\%\). The EMG exponential-tail parameter \(τ_n\) decreases strongly with photon number, while the Gaussian-location parameter \(μ_n\) continues to shift between neighboring components. A phenomenological model motivated by absorption-site-dependent vortex processes and collective current redistribution captures these timing trends. These results support wide SMSPDs as a platform for TOA-based photon-number discrimination at high photon number, relevant to multiphoton-state characterization and photonic quantum information processing. The same geometry also provides a setting to examine how the spatial distribution of photon absorption affects vortex-assisted detection.
items.why: Wide NbN microstrip detectors resolve up to eight photons from arrival-time shifts alone, with neighbouring peaks separating better at higher number.

eli5.plain: They show that a wide superconducting strip detector tells you how many photons hit it from how early it clicks, up to eight photons.
eli5.how: More photons trigger the superconducting-to-normal switch faster; in wide strips the arrival-time peaks for n and n+1 photons stay well separated instead of crowding together.
eli5.matters: Photon-number resolution from timing, with no extra readout hardware, is the same idea one wants for microwave counters; it also shows how geometry changes vortex-driven switching.
eli5.caveat: Optical photons at 515 nm and a phenomenological model; peak assignment relies on fitting, and fidelity is quoted only for adjacent pairs at equal priors.

items.title: Bias-Preserving Entanglement of Kerr-Cat Qubits with an ATS Coupler
items.abstract: Kerr-cat qubits offer a hardware-efficient route to fault-tolerant quantum computing by suppressing bit-flip errors exponentially, while phase-flip errors increase only linearly with the mean photon number. To maintain this protection, entangling operations must be bias-preserving, ensuring that phase-flip errors occurring during the gate do not propagate into bit-flip errors. In this paper, we propose an asymmetrically threaded SQUID (ATS) parametric coupler to implement high-fidelity, bias-preserving entangling gates between Kerr-cat qubits. By engineering a photon-number asymmetry between the control and target modes, we enable fast gate operations that suppress non-adiabatic leakage without complex pulse shaping. Through numerical simulations of the full circuit Hamiltonian, we demonstrate a bias-preserving CX gate achieving 99.69% fidelity in the absence of photon loss for a gate duration of 50 ns. Under a single-photon loss rate of 100 kHz, our protocol yields a noise bias of 9922, exceeding the noise bias of a naive non-bias-preserving CX implementation by approximately a factor of 570. These results support the ATS coupler as a valuable building block for concatenated cat-qubit architectures.
items.why: Simulated ATS coupler gives a 50 ns bias-preserving CX between Kerr cats at 99.69% fidelity and noise bias near 10^4.

eli5.plain: They design a coupler that entangles two cat qubits without spoiling the property that makes them attractive: bit flips stay rare.
eli5.how: An asymmetrically threaded SQUID drives a parametric interaction; using different photon numbers in control and target modes speeds the gate while avoiding leakage, without pulse shaping.
eli5.matters: Bias-preserving gates are the missing piece for concatenated cat-qubit architectures pursued by AWS and Alice&Bob; the ATS is a hardware they already use.
eli5.caveat: Numerical simulation of an idealised circuit; real devices add dephasing, thermal photons and parameter drift not modelled here.

items.title: Conservation in Every Quantum Measurement Outcome?
items.abstract: In quantum mechanics, conservation laws are usually understood only statistically and only in the context of unitary evolution: during such evolution, if an observable commutes with the Hamiltonian, its expectation value and Born-rule probability distribution remain unchanged. Individual measurement outcomes, however, disrupt even this weak form of statistical conservation. Recently, though, it has been argued that a stronger, non-statistical form of conservation, valid at the level of individual measurement outcomes, can be recovered. The proposal relies on the claim that any superposition of eigenstates of a conserved quantity must ultimately be prepared relative to another physical system, which serves as the relevant reference frame and remains correlated with the system being prepared. On this enlarged description, the change observed in the measured system is claimed to be exactly compensated by an opposite change in the preparer, thereby restoring conservation at the level of individual measurement outcomes. We analyze this proposal and argue that it faces significant conceptual difficulties. We show that the proposed mechanism is not adequately justified and, moreover, does not establish conservation in individual measurement outcomes as claimed.
items.why: Critique shows the proposed outcome-by-outcome conservation via correlated preparers is unjustified and does not deliver what it claims.

eli5.plain: They examine a recent claim that energy and other conserved quantities hold in every single measurement, not just on average, and argue it fails.
eli5.how: The claim relies on the preparing apparatus absorbing the change; they show the bookkeeping does not follow and the mechanism is not justified by the theory.
eli5.matters: Whether conservation laws survive collapse is a direct question about what measurement does, relevant to anyone reading a single-shot qubit readout as a physical event.
eli5.caveat: A critique, not a new result; defenders may refine the original proposal rather than abandon it.

items.title: All-photonic millimeter-wave and terahertz signal core at room and cryogenic temperatures
items.abstract: Millimeter-wave and terahertz technologies offer new opportunities for high-capacity communications, sensing, and quantum systems, but electronic signal chains above 100 GHz are limited by weak sources, noisy receivers, and lossy interconnects. Photonic approaches mitigate these constraints by enabling chip-scale high-frequency components, yet existing implementations generally retain lossy off-chip electrical or free-space links, hindering dense and compact integration for cryogenic or space-constrained settings. Here, we show a monolithic lithium tantalate photonic chip, termed a signal core, which generates, modulates, routes, and detects continuous-wave signals at discrete frequencies between 100 GHz and 2.5 THz. The architecture integrates high-frequency functional modules on chip and uses exclusively fiber-based optical interfaces. Bidirectional coherent electro-optic conversion enables signal generation, detection, and nanosecond-scale amplitude and phase modulation, while micro-coplanar striplines interconnect the modules into an end-to-end signal chain on a single chip. Our modules achieve single-photon electro-optic coupling rates of g_0/2π=10 kHz and peak drive-power-normalized photon-flux conversion efficiencies of 1.0%/mW for generation and 0.5%/mW for detection. It also operates at 4 K in a dilution refrigerator through the same fiber-only optical links. Together, these capabilities establish an all-photonic platform for millimeter-wave-to-terahertz systems and offer a broadly applicable architecture for applications constrained by electrical-interconnect loss, heat load, and footprint.
items.why: A lithium tantalate chip generates, modulates and detects 0.1–2.5 THz signals through fibre only, and still works at 4 K.

eli5.plain: They built a photonic chip that makes, steers and detects millimetre-wave to terahertz signals, fed only by optical fibres, and ran it inside a dilution refrigerator.
eli5.how: Electro-optic conversion turns light into high-frequency electrical signals and back, with on-chip striplines wiring the blocks together so no coax enters the cryostat.
eli5.matters: Fibre-only control of a cold stage is exactly the heat-load and wiring problem of scaling superconducting processors, and the electro-optic coupling numbers are relevant to transduction.
eli5.caveat: Conversion efficiencies near 1%/mW are far from quantum-limited, and the frequencies are above the few-GHz band superconducting qubits use.

items.title: Polarization-encoded photon statistics for counting dipole emitters
items.abstract: Counting the emitters within a diffraction-limited region is a prerequisite for localizing overlapping molecules. Under pulsed excitation, each molecule emits at most one photon per pulse, so photon-number-resolved detection can count emitters without resolving them. But the required number of pulses grows steeply with the emitter number. Here we show that polarization, conventionally used to measure the orientations of dipole emitters, also carries information on their number. Because mean polarization-resolved signals are unchanged when every emitter is replaced by multiple dimmer copies, this information resides in the photon statistics within each pulse, which polarization reshapes in two ways. Linearly polarized excitation at three angles increases the sub-Poissonian deficit of the photon count by a factor of 1.5 for any emitter orientation, and detection in four polarization channels reveals the emitter number through how the photons of multiphoton pulses are distributed among the channels. Maximum-likelihood simulations for two to five emitters of unknown orientations and brightnesses show that three-angle excitation reduces the required number of pulses by about 2.3-fold, close to the predicted $1.5^2=2.25$, and that adding four-channel detection raises the reduction to as much as 4.8-fold. These gains require only polarization optics added to photon-number-resolved detection.
items.why: Polarized excitation and four-channel detection let photon statistics count overlapping emitters with up to 4.8 times fewer pulses.

eli5.plain: They show that measuring the polarization of photons, not just how many arrive, makes it much faster to count how many molecules sit in one blurry spot.
eli5.how: Each molecule gives at most one photon per pulse; polarized excitation deepens the sub-Poissonian dip, and how multi-photon pulses split across polarization channels reveals the emitter number.
eli5.matters: It is a clean example of extracting emitter number from photon-number statistics by adding a mode degree of freedom, a trick that carries to counting artificial atoms in a waveguide.
eli5.caveat: Simulations only, for two to five emitters, assuming good photon-number-resolving detectors.

items.title: Mutual Information Across Quantum Reference Frame Perspectives
items.abstract: In quantum information theory, standard notions typically presuppose a fixed partition of the world into subsystems, encoded in a tensor product structure of the Hilbert space. Yet, in some scenarios, the subsystem structure is not uniquely fixed. A case in point is the description of subsystems relative to different quantum reference frames (QRFs), where the tensor product structure, although fixed in a specific QRF, changes across different QRFs. Such a relativity of subsystems underlies many interesting features of QRFs, such as the relativity of entanglement, entropy, and coherence. It also raises a broader question: how do we compare the information across different subsystem perspectives, especially when the corresponding subsystem algebras overlap? Here, we propose a notion of quantum mutual information across different QRF perspectives, which captures the correlations between subsystems relative to different frames of reference. To do so, we focus on an algebraic definition of subsystems. Studying in detail the union and overlap between subsystem algebras relative to different QRFs, we find that the usual definition of mutual information in terms of the chain law overcounts the information associated to the overlap. Based on this insight, we propose a modified chain law and show that the resulting notion of mutual information satisfies subadditivity and connects naturally to other measures found in the literature [1]. Our investigations not only provide a way to quantify the relation between different QRF perspectives from an information-theoretic point of view but also sheds light on some important features of quantum information in absence of a fixed tensor product structure.
items.why: Defines mutual information between subsystems seen from different quantum reference frames, correcting overcounting via a modified chain rule.

eli5.plain: They define how much two observers using different quantum reference frames 'share' information, when they disagree about how the world splits into parts.
eli5.how: Subsystems are defined by operator algebras; when algebras from two frames overlap, the usual chain rule double-counts, so they modify it and recover subadditivity.
eli5.matters: It addresses why the tensor-product split is not given a priori, which bears on what entanglement between a qubit and its environment even means.
eli5.caveat: Information-theoretic and definitional; it proposes a measure rather than proving something about the physical world.

items.title: Nanopillar metasurfaces uniting high optical reflectivity with ultracoherent nanomechanics
items.abstract: Mechanically compliant mirrors are key components in cavity optomechanics. However, the requirements to achieve the best optical and mechanical performance are usually in direct competition. A high reflectivity for tightly focused beams entails thick reflectors, whereas ultracoherent flexural nanomechanics necessitates thin membranes. We eliminate this trade-off by introducing high-refractive-index nanopillar metasurfaces on top of a thin membrane. We pattern a 50 micrometer-diameter array of nanopillars to form a photonic crystal. The flat band behavior of guided resonances in the photonic crystal enables a reflectivity of 99.82(1)% for a tightly focused beam of 7 micrometer waist. The combination of two guided resonances creates a 100 nanometer-wide high-reflectivity band around 1550 nanometer. Simultaneously, the nanopillar patterning realizes a density-modulated phononic crystal that isolates an ultracoherent localized mechanical mode with a $Q\cdot f$-product of $2\cdot 10^{14}$Hz. The demonstrated nanopillar metasurfaces enable lightweight mirrors for room-temperature quantum optomechanics and for use as levitated mirrors or lightsails.
items.why: Nanopillar metasurface on a thin membrane reaches 99.82% reflectivity while hosting a mechanical mode with Q·f of 2×10^14 Hz.

eli5.plain: They made a mirror that is both highly reflective and a very clean mechanical resonator, two goals that usually fight each other.
eli5.how: Pillars on a thin membrane form a photonic crystal that reflects a tightly focused beam, while the same pattern acts as a phononic crystal that isolates one low-loss vibration mode.
eli5.matters: Ultracoherent membranes are candidates for microwave-optical transducers and mechanical memories coupled to superconducting circuits.
eli5.caveat: Demonstrated at 1550 nm and room temperature; no cavity optomechanics or quantum-regime operation is shown yet.

items.title: Attosecond Quantum Optical Spectroscopy of Topological Materials
items.abstract: High-harmonic generation (HHG) provides an ultrafast probe of quantum materials, yet conventional spectral observables do not generally furnish a common signature of band topology. Here we show that quantum-light-driven HHG opens an additional information channel through the photon statistics of the emitted harmonics. Using the Haldane Chern insulator and the time-reversal-invariant Kane-Mele topological insulator, we calculate helicity-resolved equal-time intensity correlations and identify a common enhancement of high-order harmonic correlations in the topological phases. For the Haldane model, a dichroic correlation constructed from opposite helicity channels reverses sign with the Chern number. These signatures originate from the distinct nonlinear response sampled by quantum fluctuations of the driving field and are absent from the corresponding mean harmonic spectra as a common classifier. Our results establish photon-correlation spectroscopy as a route to interrogate topological matter with quantum light and provide a bridge between strong-field solid-state physics and quantum optics.
items.why: Harmonics driven by quantum light carry intensity correlations that flip sign with the Chern number, absent from the mean spectrum.

eli5.plain: They predict that the photon statistics of high harmonics, generated in a material by quantum light, can reveal whether the material is topological.
eli5.how: Fluctuations of a non-classical drive sample the material's nonlinear response; correlations between helicity channels pick up the band topology even when average spectra do not.
eli5.matters: It is an example of photon correlations as a probe that mean intensities miss, the same logic as g2 measurements on circuit emitters.
eli5.caveat: Model calculations on idealised lattice models; the needed bright quantum drives for HHG and correlation measurements at high harmonics are experimentally hard.

items.title: The Four-Qubit Hyperbolic Quadric Has Contextuality Degree 315
items.abstract: The contextuality degree of a set of Pauli contexts is the least number of contexts that every noncontextual $\pm1$ assignment violates. For the four-qubit hyperbolic quadric $\mathcal{Q}^{+}(7,2)$, with $135$ points and $1575$ lines as contexts, Muller et al. conjectured from heuristic searches that the degree is $315$ and that the violated contexts of every optimal assignment form a dual polar space $DW(5,2)$. We prove both conjectures. The lower bound has a short proof by hand: every doily ($GQ(2,2)$) of the quadric contains ten Peres-Mermin grids covering each of its lines four times, so every assignment violates at least three of its fifteen lines, and averaging over the doilies gives $1575/5=315$. The equality case is local: an assignment is optimal exactly when it violates one ruling of one grid in every doily. Using this as a SAT encoding, we show that there are exactly $240$ optimal violated sets, one orbit of $\mathrm{O}^+(8,2)$, each isomorphic to $DW(5,2)$. The same argument gives the first lower bounds $\lceil L/5\rceil$ for all quadrics with $L$ lines in $N\ge4$ qubits. The degree theorem is kernel-checked in Lean 4, and the completeness of the enumeration is certified by a DRAT proof checked by the verified checker cake_lpr.
items.why: Proves the four-qubit hyperbolic quadric has contextuality degree 315, with a hand proof plus Lean and DRAT certificates.

eli5.plain: They prove exactly how badly any classical, pre-assigned-values model must fail for a specific large set of four-qubit Pauli measurements.
eli5.how: Each sub-structure contains Peres–Mermin grids forcing at least three violations; averaging gives the lower bound 315, and a SAT search shows all optimal patterns are one symmetric family.
eli5.matters: A sharp contextuality count gives a target for experiments testing noncontextual hidden variables on multi-qubit processors.
eli5.caveat: Mostly a combinatorial result; its physical reading is the standard Kochen–Specker one, and noise thresholds for an experiment are not derived.

items.title: Photon localization: Local measurements, localized states, and causality
items.abstract: We review what it means for a relativistic particle to be localized and argue that the most useful approach is through local measurement. This perspective ties localization directly to relativistic causality and measurable outcomes in spacetime. Strict localization in quantum field theory is formalized by states that give the same expectation value as vacuum for all local observables outside some spacetime region. With this formalism, single photons cannot be strictly localized, but coherent states can. The structure and interpretation of local observables and local operator algebras are discussed in connection with the Reeh-Schlieder theorem. Since probabilities of local measurement outcomes cannot vanish in vacuum, particle detection events must be phrased carefully. Key characteristics of strictly localized states are surveyed alongside concrete strategies for constructing them. The relationship between localization, causality, and on-demand sources is analyzed, finding that strictly localized states can represent localized, propagating information in quantum field theory. Explicit examples of localized photonic states are presented with an emphasis on quantum optics, including states that approximate single photons and (entangled) Bell states.
items.why: Review argues localization must be defined by local measurements: single photons cannot be strictly localized, coherent states can.

eli5.plain: A review of what it means for a photon to be 'somewhere', built on what local detectors can measure rather than on wavefunctions.
eli5.how: A state is strictly localized if it looks like vacuum to every measurement outside a region; quantum field theory forbids this for single photons but allows it for coherent states.
eli5.matters: Anyone who emits or catches 'a single photon in a wavepacket' uses this language loosely; the review says which statements about on-demand sources survive relativistic causality.
eli5.caveat: A review and conceptual reframing; it adds no new measurement and the operational consequences for lab sources are qualitative.

items.title: Time-reversal-based quantum metrology in a central-spin architecture: from SATIN to butterfly echo
items.abstract: We investigate quantum-enhanced time-reversal-based metrology using the central spin model, in which a single ancilla spin of magnitude $S_{\rm cen}$ mediates interactions between $N$ bath spins through a star-graph topology. We demonstrate that the SATIN (Signal Amplification Through Time-reversal Interaction) echo protocol can be implemented in this setup to achieve a Fisher information of $N^2/e$ with the collective $\langle J_y\rangle$ readout, corresponding to a $4.34\,\mathrm{dB}$ offset from the Heisenberg limit. Furthermore, we establish that this platform provides a pathway to perform the butterfly echo protocol by conjugating each evolution step with a random collective bath rotation, thereby achieving axis-agnostic Heisenberg-scaled sensing. Crucially, with a small $N-$independent number of random steps, the butterfly echo reaches a Fisher information of $N^2/4$ ($6\,\mathrm{dB}$ below the Heisenberg limit) for any unknown encoding axis, with the plateau gain tracking the Haar limit. Finally, we demonstrate that the central-spin magnitude $S_{\rm cen}$ provides a powerful knob to reduce the optimal protocol timescale without altering the metrological ceiling or the circuit depth required to reach isotropy. The proposed scheme is relevant to cavity QED and NMR quantum processors, where the central spin architecture arises naturally.
items.why: A central spin mediating a star-shaped bath implements SATIN and butterfly echoes reaching Heisenberg-scaled sensing for any unknown axis.

eli5.plain: They show a sensing protocol that runs time forward and backward through a single central spin to reach near-ideal precision with many bath spins.
eli5.how: Interactions go through one ancilla; reversing them amplifies a small signal, and random collective rotations make it work whatever direction the signal points.
eli5.matters: A qubit coupled to many modes or spins via a common bus is a circuit QED geometry, so the protocol could transfer to a transmon coupled to a spin ensemble.
eli5.caveat: Purely theoretical and noiseless; decoherence and imperfect time reversal will eat into the 4–6 dB offsets quoted.

items.title: \textit{In situ} certification of multiparticle indistinguishability in a generic interferometer
items.abstract: We propose a scalable and efficient \textit{in situ} method for assessing the multiparticle indistinguishability of identical bosons or fermions in quantum interference experiments on linear interferometers by harnessing quantum parallelism and the bunching/anti-bunching tendencies of these particles. The proposed certification method can be applied to any generic linear interferometer. For particles occupying distinct input ports of a Haar-random unitary interferometer, the number of experimental runs required to attain a prescribed statistical precision is polynomial in the number of particles, the interferometer size, and the inverse precision, with high probability. Our method is robust under losses: for uniform particle losses, the polynomial scaling is preserved when the inverse single-particle survival probability is polynomially bounded. Our scheme is especially suitable for certifying the indistinguishability of single photons in large-scale interference experiments, such as Boson Sampling in the regime of quantum advantage over classical computation.
items.why: Bunching statistics in any random interferometer certify multiphoton indistinguishability with polynomial runs, even under uniform loss.

eli5.plain: They propose a quick test, run on the experiment itself, of how identical the photons in a big interference experiment really are.
eli5.how: Identical bosons bunch together more than distinguishable ones; averaging bunching signatures over a generic interferometer gives an indistinguishability estimate with polynomial sampling cost.
eli5.matters: Certifying identical photons in situ matters for any multi-photon microwave interference experiment too, where indistinguishability is usually inferred indirectly.
eli5.caveat: The polynomial guarantee is with high probability for Haar-random interferometers and uniform loss; structured devices and nonuniform loss are not covered.

items.title: Moments of Random Permanents and Hafnians: A Replica Approach
items.abstract: Using contour-integral representations of the permanent and of the Hafnian, we turn the computation of their moments for random matrices into a replica calculation, analogous to that of the moments of the partition function of a mean-field spin glass. For the $2k$-th moment of $N\times N$ matrices with independent entries, the dominant saddle point is replica symmetric for $k>2$, and we obtain in closed form the exponential growth rate, the prefactor and the first $1/N$ correction, in agreement with exact enumerations. The growth rate depends only on whether the entries are real or complex; higher cumulants affect only the prefactor and the $1/N$ term. At $k=2$ the replica-symmetric solution becomes unstable, separating a power-law bulk of the distribution from a large-deviation tail, which we compute. The results apply to boson sampling with single photons and with squeezed light.
items.why: Replica calculation gives closed-form growth rates and corrections for moments of random permanents and hafnians, relevant to boson sampling.

items.title: Single-photon time qubit: Quantum-vacuum control and complementarity of the arrow of time
items.abstract: Treating the arrow of time as a controllable quantum variable rather than a fixed external parameter is a central challenge in quantum physics. Recently, Bloch~\cite{Bloch2025} proposed the theoretical concept of a \emph{time qubit}, a two-level control space $\mathcal{H}_T=\mathrm{span}\{\ket{+},\ket{-}\}$ that selects between opposite Hamiltonian evolutions $\hat{H}_{\pm}=\hat{H}_0\pm\hat{V}$, but this paradigm has remained experimentally unrealized. Here we formulate the quantum-optical theory of a single-photon time qubit---uncovering quantum-vacuum control and complementarity of the arrow of time---and experimentally probe and validate its predictions using phase-resolved single-photon interferometry from two coherently seeded entangled nonlinear biphoton sources~\cite{Lee2018,Yoon2021}. First, we show theoretically and verify experimentally that a controlled $π$ pump--seed phase inversion during pair creation from the quantum vacuum flips the stimulated displacement generator $\hat{V}\to -\hat{V}$ on top of the spontaneous two-mode squeezing background $\hat{H}_0$, reversing the stimulated evolution time [$\hat{U}_{\mathrm{stim},-}(t)=\hat{U}_{\mathrm{stim},+}(-t)$] and enabling universal single-qubit $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ control and postselection-free first-order tomography on the temporal Bloch sphere. Second, we prove that spontaneous idler vacuum fluctuations record complete which-branch (temporal-direction) information whereas the shared coherent seed erases it without cascading or aligning the idler beams, establishing an exact wave--particle complementarity law $|\bm{r}|=\mathcal{V}=|α|^2/(1+|α|^2)$ for the purity of the arrow of time and enabling direct first-order measurement of the Loschmidt time-reversal echo.
items.why: Phase inversion in seeded biphoton sources flips the stimulated evolution, giving a controllable two-level 'time qubit' with a complementarity law.

items.title: Allight: A Perfect Photon Collector
items.abstract: Collecting photons from quantum emitters remains a key limitation in light-matter interaction because conventional lenses collect light only from one direction. Here, we introduce a perfect light collector by inverse-designing a surrounding dielectric structure that encloses the emitter to increase photon-collection efficiency toward unity. Decomposing the device into several refractive interfaces enables emission collection from the full 4$π$ solid angle with adiabatic reshaping into a collimated beam. We experimentally demonstrate, in two dimensions, the ray bending that collimates omnidirectional emission. Our collector transforms current paradigms for highly efficient photon collection from narrowband, cavity-based techniques into experimentally robust, broadband, non-resonant dielectric devices.
items.why: Inverse-designed dielectric enclosure collects emission from the full 4π solid angle into one beam; ray bending demonstrated only in 2D.

items.title: Phonon-assisted free-electron recoil control and mechanical sensing
items.abstract: Mechanical vibrations are fundamental to a wide range of physical phenomena and technologies, yet their ability to actively shape free-electron dynamics remains largely unexplored. Here we theoretically show how an optomechanical membrane provides a phonon-assisted optical interface for controlling free-electron recoil and sensing localized forces. Transverse membrane motion scatters cavity light into high-momentum evanescent sidebands that enable phase-matched interaction with electrons traveling in vacuum. Beyond supplying momentum for phase matching, the vibration amplitude controls the electron-light interaction strength and redistributes electron populations among recoil orders. External forces that perturb the vibration are thereby encoded in the electron recoil spectrum. Under the modeled conditions, electron readout of localized stochastic forces can yield a higher signal-to-noise ratio than a Gaussian optical homodyne benchmark at equal detected probe rates. These results provide a theoretical basis for mechanically reconfigurable free-electron optics and mode-selective mechanical sensing.
items.why: Membrane vibrations scatter cavity light into evanescent sidebands that steer free-electron recoil and read out localized forces.

items.title: Quantum theory of laser noise in coherent-scattering levitated optomechanics
items.abstract: State purity is a key resource for experimental tests of quantum mechanics with massive objects. Cavity cooling of a levitated nanoparticle via coherent scattering stands out as a strategy to prepare highly pure states of its roto-translational motion. In several cases, though, the performance of cooling by coherent scattering is limited by the classical fluctuations of the laser field. Here we present a quantum theory of coherent-scattering experiments which includes the effect of the laser amplitude and phase noise. We derive a master equation for the noise-averaged particle's dynamics, valid for both center-of-mass and rotational degrees of freedom, and quantify the cooling performance for different levels of noise in state-of-the-art experiments. We compute approximate analytical expressions for the laser-noise-induced heating rates and excess phonon number in both regimes of weak and strong optomechanical coupling. Moreover, our model can be applied to laser noise processes with generic power spectral densities and finite correlation times. This work offers a toolbox to quantify and optimize the state purity in coherent-scattering experiments, and opens new avenues towards the preparation of quantum states with levitated systems.
items.why: Master equation for laser amplitude and phase noise sets heating rates and phonon floors in coherent-scattering cooling of nanoparticles.

items.title: Entanglement Distribution in Quantum Switch Networks: Memory Limits and Achievability
items.abstract: We study the minimum persistent memory required to distribute a graph state through a quantum switch. Specifically, consider a central switch that assists $n$ remote users in distributing a graph state, using independently generated user-switch Bell pairs. Since Bell-pair generation is probabilistic, different links generally succeed at different times. When a Bell-pair is generated, the qubits may need to be stored in memory while waiting for other links to succeed. Recently, new protocols have been proposed to reduce this storage overhead by processing and releasing some switch qubits before all Bell links are available. However, these protocols do not characterize the minimum persistent switch memory required at each stage. Moreover, the local-cover method in the state-of-the-art Piecemaker protocol is computationally expensive for general target graphs. In this work, we characterize the minimum persistent switch memory required after any subset of users' Bell links are generated and processed. We then develop an online stabilizer-transition protocol that attains this limit, which can be implemented in polynomial time in the number of qubits $n$. Remarkably, this optimal protocol can provide substantial memory reductions over existing heuristic approaches. In particular, for the path graph $P_n$ over $n$ users, Piecemaker protocol requires at least $\lfloor n/2\rfloor$ qubits of peak persistent memory for \textit{every Bell-links generation order}, whereas under the order $(1,2,\ldots,n)$, our protocol requires only one persistent switch qubit. Finally, the same stabilizer-transition framework also provides a direct forward construction for sequential graph-state generation using the minimum number of quantum emitters, equal to the maximum of the height function.
items.why: Characterises minimum switch memory for graph-state distribution and gives a polynomial protocol needing one qubit for a path graph.

items.title: Single-step SU(3) Hahn Echo in a Qutrit Atom Interferometer
items.abstract: The Hahn echo is a well-known dynamical decoupling method that refocuses the dephasing due to energy inhomogeneities of a spin-1/2 ensemble and is widely used to extend phase coherence in quantum computers and sensors. Extensions of such techniques beyond the spin-1/2 have been reported, but have mainly used SU(2) gates, limiting their scalability. Here, we generalize the Hahn echo to qutrits using single-step SU(3) gates and extend the coherence time by more than an order of magnitude. The gates are generated through optimal control theory and implemented in an ultracold atomic ensemble in free fall. A quantum process tomography procedure benchmarks the gates and yields fidelities of ~ 93%, limited mainly by state preparation and measurement errors. Due to the geometry of the laser beams, the generalized Hahn echo also realizes a three-path Mach-Zehnder atomic interferometer with two independent interferometric phase differences. Our results therefore establish SU(3) control for dynamical decoupling of qutrits and multi-path atom interferometers, with the latter opening the possibility for vector force measurements and interferometric tests of the validity of Born's rule.
items.why: Single-step SU(3) gates give a qutrit Hahn echo extending coherence tenfold and form a three-path atom interferometer.

eli5.plain: They extended the classic spin echo trick to three-level atoms in free fall, keeping them coherent ten times longer and making a three-arm interferometer.
eli5.how: Optimal-control laser pulses rotate all three levels at once, refocusing dephasing; the beam geometry makes the sequence a three-path Mach–Zehnder interferometer.
eli5.matters: Three-path interference is the setting where Born's rule could be tested for higher-order interference; this builds the instrument.
eli5.caveat: No Born-rule test is performed yet; gate fidelity is about 93%.

items.title: Noise-Assisted Quantum Entanglement: Memory-Enhanced Coherence in Stochastic Jaynes-Cummings Dynamics
items.abstract: We investigate qubit entanglement dynamics in a two-qubit cavity system with stochastically fluctuating coupling strength, comparing white noise (Markovian) and Ornstein-Uhlenbeck noise (non-Markovian) processes. We analytically solve the system dynamics for both Fock and coherent cavity states and systematically characterize how initial qubit configurations affect entanglement generation and preservation. Our results reveal distinct dynamical regimes: in the Fock-state cavity, initial states in the single-excitation subspace generate robust qubit entanglement in decoherence-free subspaces, while initially entangled states in the double-excitation subspace exhibit inevitable decay without protective symmetries. For coherent cavities, we identify a critical photon-number threshold in the intermediate coherent-state amplitude regime where dynamics transition from low-frequency to high-frequency entanglement oscillations, while universal entanglement loss occurs at large amplitudes. Remarkable resilience against entanglement sudden death emerges under strong non-Markovian noise with long correlation times, where repeated revivals occur. These findings establish cavity photon statistics and environmental memory time as key control parameters for engineering qubit entanglement dynamics in qubit-cavity systems, revealing how system-environment correlations govern quantum information preservation.
items.why: Non-Markovian coupling noise in a two-qubit Jaynes–Cummings model produces entanglement revivals and resists sudden death.

items.title: Controlling Optical Quantum Interference with Plasmonic Metasurfaces
items.abstract: The ability to efficiently control optical quantum interference by the same device is a challenging task that promises to enable key operations in quantum information processing. Here, we tackle this problem by presenting a composite quantum plasmonic metasurface operating as an ultrathin non-unitary beamsplitter capable of achieving both single photon bosonic bunching and fermionic anti-bunching interference just by varying the incident photons frequency or changing the design dimensions. The presented metasurface combines a plasmonic grating corrugated by periodic nanoslits that can achieve extraordinary optical transmission with additional nanostripes on top forming nanocavities characterized by localized gap plasmon resonances. The photon-photon interactions are analyzed based on calculating the quantum coalescence metric which accurately portrays the obtained bunching or anti-bunching quantum interference. The presented quantum interference operation is applicable to both fundamental non-classical light interactions and in the design of more applied quantum optical logic gates used in quantum computing and communications.
items.why: Simulated plasmonic metasurface switches two-photon interference between bunching and antibunching by frequency or geometry.

items.title: A Personal History in Quantum Foundations: an Oral History Interview
items.abstract: This oral history interview provides Yakir Aharonov's personal and conceptual recollections from the 1950s to the 2000s, focusing on his academic trajectory, some of his major contributions to quantum foundations, and his perspective on the development of the field. The interview traces Aharonov's academic career through the Technion, University of Bristol, Brandeis University, Yeshiva University, University of South Carolina, Tel Aviv University, George Mason University, and Chapman University. The interview also traces the development of Aharonov's work and collaborations on the EPR paradox, time-energy uncertainty relations, quantum measurement theory, quantum frames of reference, the two-state vector formalism, weak values, protective measurements, and several other contributions. It includes recollections of meetings and discussions with David Bohm, Niels Bohr, John Clauser, Paul Dirac, Rudolf Peierls, Aage Petersen, and Abner Shimony. Also mentioned: David Albert, Jeeva Anandan, Peter Bergmann, Gideon Carmi, Avshalom Elitzur, Dave Finkelstein, Vladimir Fock, Itzhak Kalugai, Ed Lerner, Joel Lebowitz, Stanley Mandelstam, Yuval Ne'eman, Sandu Popescu, Maurice Pryce, Daniel Rohrlich, Nathan Rosen, Joseph Safko, Paul Singer, Daniele Struppa, Leonard Susskind, Lev Vaidman, Chien-Shiung Wu.
items.why: Oral history of Yakir Aharonov's career, from EPR and time-energy uncertainty to weak values and protective measurement.

eli5.plain: An interview in which Yakir Aharonov recounts how his main ideas in quantum foundations came about.
eli5.how: A historian guides him through his career and collaborations, with recollections of Bohm, Bohr, Dirac and others.
eli5.matters: It gives context for weak values and the two-state vector formalism, which are often used to interpret weak measurements in circuit QED.
eli5.caveat: Personal recollection, not argument; nothing new is claimed about the physics.

items.title: Fidelity Dynamics of a Jaynes--Cummings Qubit under Markovian and Non-Markovian Coupling Noise
items.abstract: We analytically investigate the fidelity dynamics of a Jaynes--Cummings qubit coupled to a single-mode cavity in the presence of stochastic fluctuations of the qubit--cavity coupling. Such fluctuations naturally arise in cavity- and circuit-QED platforms due to fabrication imperfections, control-field noise, mechanical vibrations, and environmental disturbances. Since the qubit--cavity coupling governs the rate of coherent energy and information exchange, understanding the effects of its fluctuations is essential for assessing the performance of quantum communication, quantum sensing, and quantum information-processing protocols. We consider both Gaussian white noise and Ornstein--Uhlenbeck noise with finite correlation time as models for the coupling fluctuations. Exploiting the closed dynamics within each excitation manifold, we derive exact analytical expressions for the noise-averaged density matrix and the fidelity relative to the ideal noiseless evolution. We show that the fidelity is determined by a single decoherence factor governed by the integrated noise correlation function, establishing a direct connection between microscopic coupling fluctuations and macroscopic coherence loss. In the white-noise limit, the fidelity decays exponentially, whereas finite noise correlation times produce nonexponential decay and slower coherence loss. We further show that the crossover between Markovian-like and non-Markovian regimes is controlled by the ratio of the noise correlation rate to the coherent coupling strength, and that decoherence increases with photon number because of the enhanced effective qubit--cavity coupling. These results provide a unified analytical framework for quantifying decoherence induced by stochastic coupling fluctuations and for evaluating the robustness of cavity-QED protocols under correlated noise.
items.why: Exact fidelity under fluctuating qubit–cavity coupling depends on one decoherence factor set by the integrated noise correlation.

items.title: Minimal-length kinematics of coherent light and a proposed two-color vacuum chronoscopy
items.abstract: The unification of quantum theory and general relativity suggests the existence of a minimal measurable length, leading to a generalized uncertainty principle (GUP) and an energy-dependent vacuum group velocity. Testing these effects with macroscopic objects typically encounters the ``soccer-ball problem,'' where applying Planck-scale deformations to the total momentum predicts observationally ruled-out velocity deviations. We adopt the QFT-natural prescription in which the GUP modifies single-mode commutators, and verify by explicit calculation that the macroscopic group velocity of a multimode coherent pulse reduces to the single-photon GUP velocity evaluated at the central wavelength, multiplied by the classical Gaussian-beam factor, with no dependence on the total pulse energy. The energy--momentum relation $E=pc$ itself is unmodified; the deformation enters through the velocity--momentum relation and is equivalent to a modified dispersion relation in the wave vector, with a quadratic coefficient that depends on which of the two variables is used. The soccer-ball problem $\,$---$\,$ which arises only when the GUP is applied to the center-of-mass momentum of a composite system $\,$---$\,$ is therefore absent for coherent light, and macroscopic petawatt pulses probe the same parameter space as single high-energy photons. Building on this framework, we propose a two-color vacuum chronoscopy experiment using a short-pulse petawatt laser and its high-harmonic generation. By systematically varying the macroscopic beam waist, our setup separates Planck-scale kinematic shifts from classical diffraction delays, establishing a controlled, source-independent terrestrial methodology whose sensitivity we assess against current astrophysical bounds and against the dominant waist-independent systematics that limit it, residual-gas dispersion and the harmonic birth-time offset.
items.why: Argues the soccer-ball problem vanishes for coherent light and proposes a petawatt two-colour delay test of minimal-length physics.

items.title: Teaching quantum mechanics in secondary schools: A qubit-first learning path to Bell's inequalities
items.abstract: Teaching quantum mechanics at the secondary school level remains a major educational challenge. Traditional historical approaches often present the theory as a sequence of disconnected phenomena, requiring extensive prior knowledge of classical physics before students can appreciate the conceptual structure of quantum physics. In this work, we present the design, implementation, and evaluation of a curriculum based on the two state (qubit first) approach, in which the fundamental postulates of quantum mechanics are introduced through mathematically accessible two level systems and realized with light polarization. The curriculum integrates theoretical instruction, laboratory activities, a coherent progression grounded in the interactive simulations, and inquiry based learning into a coherent pathway that progresses from quantum states and superposition to entanglement and the experimental violation of Bell's inequalities. A distinctive feature of the project is the experimental realization of the violation of Bell's inequalities obtained in a newly established quantum optics laboratory in an Italian high school, where students performed, for the first time in Italy, an authentic Bell test using polarization-entangled photons. The same educational framework was adopted for in service teacher professional development courses. Learning outcomes were evaluated through mixed methods. Preliminary analysis indicates significant improvements in conceptual understanding, confidence in using mathematical formalism, and appreciation of the relationship between theory, experimentation, and the foundations of quantum mechanics. The proposed curriculum shows that two-state formalism and supported by real laboratory experiences enables secondary-school students to engage more meaningfully with both the conceptual foundations of quantum mechanics and their experimental verification.
items.why: High-school students perform a real polarization-entangled Bell test within a qubit-first curriculum.

eli5.plain: A school curriculum teaches quantum mechanics starting from qubits, ending with students running their own Bell test with entangled photons.
eli5.how: Light polarization stands in for a qubit; lessons, simulations and a school optics lab build up from superposition to entanglement and Bell violation.
eli5.matters: Mainly educational; it shows Bell tests are now a teaching experiment.
eli5.caveat: Learning outcomes are preliminary, and the Bell test itself adds nothing new to foundations.

items.title: Resolving Nonlocal State Reduction via Induced Coherence in Frequency-Comb Biphoton Sources
items.abstract: How macroscopic definite outcomes and nonlocal correlations emerge from entangled superpositions across spacelike-separated regions without superluminal action or {\it ad hoc} wavefunction collapse remains a defining open question in the foundations of quantum mechanics. Here, we resolve this century-long paradox within \textit{linear} relativistic quantum electrodynamics by developing an open-system and measurement-defined framework realized in dual, spacelike-separated nonlinear crystals driven synchronously by a multi-mode optical frequency comb and seeded by an ultra-narrow coherent laser. Expanding the transverse electromagnetic vector potential into discrete single-photon frequency-comb supermodes, we show that tracing out the unmeasured continuous-wave idler field yields an exact spatial dephasing Lindblad master equation whose decoherence rate is governed by the non-orthogonal state overlap of single-photon-added coherent states. Connecting this open-system map to free-vector-space quotient measurement theory, we demonstrate that single-particle interference arises from the geometric projection of the composite state onto detector-defined conditional cosets rather than remote collapse, establishing strict operational equivalence across pump, seed, and signal phase scans. The resulting wave-particle-entanglement triality equality $P^2 + E^2 + V^2 = 1$ is saturated across the complete parameter space, while the atomic-clock-referenced comb structure anchors continuous-variable time-frequency displacement stabilizers directly at the hardware layer. Our work unifies induced coherence, Bohr's complementarity, and quotient measurement theory, providing a microscopic pathway toward fault-tolerant bosonic quantum information processing.
items.why: Claims to resolve nonlocal state reduction in linear QED via induced coherence in seeded comb biphoton sources, without engaging existing no-go results.

eli5.plain: The author claims a framework that explains how definite outcomes and nonlocal correlations arise without collapse, using a specific optical setup.
eli5.how: Tracing out an unmeasured seeded field gives a dephasing master equation, and interference is re-described as projection onto detector-defined classes.
eli5.matters: It recasts induced coherence and complementarity, but its bearing on the measurement problem is asserted rather than shown.
eli5.caveat: Decoherence after tracing out a mode is standard and does not by itself solve the measurement problem; the broad claim does not engage the existing literature.

items.title: Hidden Perturbative Structure in Attosecond Streaking
items.abstract: Attosecond streaking is inherently multiphoton, yet we uncover a hidden perturbative structure revealing the underlying continuum--continuum angular-momentum propensity. By filtering the inversion-odd response in helium streaking data at the IR fundamental, we isolate an angular distribution dominated by the $P_1$ and $P_3$ Legendre components, whose complex coefficients yield an effective $s/d$ two-photon amplitude ratio. Multichannel, two-electron time-dependent Schrödinger equation calculations demonstrate that the characteristic Fano propensity survives electron correlation. Incorporating the experimental XUV attochirp reproduces the measured emission-edge trend, while near-threshold calculations predict resonant amplitude and phase signatures associated with the bound He $np$ Rydberg series. This symmetry- and frequency-filtering approach offers a general spectroscopic framework with potential applications to atomic, molecular, and solid-state systems where attosecond streaking is established.
items.why: Filtering helium streaking data isolates a perturbative two-photon s/d amplitude ratio hidden in the multiphoton signal.

items.title: Atmospheric channel model for QKD over satellite megaconstellations
items.abstract: Atmospheric turbulence and channel loss represent the primary limiting factors in ground-to-satellite quantum communication systems, yet their joint impact remains insufficiently characterized across diverse operational conditions. In this work, we develop a comprehensive and open atmospheric channel model for quantum optical links along ground-to-satellite paths, integrating altitude-dependent molecular and aerosol absorptions. The model is validated with available data from missions such as Micius and Hispasat, including a secondary viability assessment for a hypothetical Starlink-based quantum communication network, where we evaluate the predicted channel behavior in terms of single-photon transmittance and power balance, alongside the channel capacity of the link for uplink and downlink exclusively. Our comparative analysis demonstrates the ability of our channel model to predict real data under simple atmospheric behavior assumptions, which offer practical guidelines for the design and optimization of future quantum satellite missions.
items.why: Open atmospheric channel model for ground-to-satellite QKD, validated against Micius and Hispasat, applied to a Starlink scenario.

items.title: Symmetry and Quantum Interference in the Attosecond Domain
items.abstract: In this review, we examine the interplay of symmetry and quantum interference in the attosecond domain primarily through one- and two-electron photoelectron momentum distributions. Using our own work, we discuss how tailored laser fields provide control over dynamical symmetries, and how quantum-orbit methods make it possible to connect the resulting momentum-space structures to specific ionisation, propagation, and rescattering pathways. Particular emphasis is placed on ultrafast photoelectron holography and nonsequential double ionisation through recollision excitation with subsequent ionisation, where several distinct forms of quantum interference can be identified and manipulated. We also discuss how target properties, including the binding potential, orbital symmetry and parity, modify this mapping. Finally, we consider emerging opportunities offered by non-classical states of light, for which photon statistics and quantum fluctuations provide additional degrees of freedom for controlling symmetry and strong-field electron dynamics.
items.why: Review of symmetry and interference in strong-field photoelectron momentum distributions, with an outlook on non-classical drives.

items.title: Quantum Machine Learning in Medical Imaging: A Primer for Radiologists
items.abstract: Deep learning has transformed radiology, but the computational cost of training and deploying modern models is outpacing what classical hardware can support. Quantum computing has been proposed as one response to this bottleneck: an n-qubit system can represent $2^n$ states simultaneously, although practical speedups require efficient algorithms, data encoding, and measurement strategies rather than superposition alone. This review introduces radiologists to five core quantum concepts, qubits, superposition, entanglement, quantum gates, and quantum circuits, and to the superconducting, trapped-ion, and photonic hardware platforms that define the current noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) era. We then summarize the quantum machine learning architectures most often applied to medical imaging (quantum support vector machines, quantum neural networks, variational quantum circuits, and quantum convolutional neural networks) and quantum image representations such as the flexible representation of quantum images (FRQI) and the novel enhanced quantum representation (NEQR). Reported applications include brain tumor classification and segmentation on MRI, pneumonia detection on chest radiographs, skin and breast lesion classification, CT and PET reconstruction, and ultrasound denoising. Nearly all published systems are hybrid quantum-classical pipelines evaluated on small, downsampled benchmark datasets or simulators, and clinical deployment is not yet feasible. We conclude with current limitations and translational priorities for radiology.
items.why: Introductory review of quantum machine learning for radiologists; reported medical results are small-scale simulations.

items.title: Mamba Quantum Eigensolver (MQE): A Selective State Space Model for Scalable Ground State Simulations in Quantum Chemistry
items.abstract: Predicting molecular electronic structure using Quantum Computing approaches is a challenge in Computational Chemistry. Traditional Variational Quantum Eigensolvers (VQEs) are typically hindered by optimization challenges. The alternative Generative Quantum Eigensolver (GQE) mitigates this by reformulating ground-state search as discrete sequence generation, but its Transformer backbone suffers from quadratic computational complexity, bottlenecking scalability for larger molecules. To address this, we introduce the Mamba Quantum Eigensolver (Mamba-QE), which replaces the Transformer with a Selective State Space Model (SSM) to process operator sequences with linear $\mathcal{O}(L)$ complexity. Additionally, we integrate a distance-conditioned mechanism enabling the direct prediction of complete potential energy surfaces (PES). Evaluated on the $H_2$ molecule, Mamba-QE reproduces Full Configuration Interaction (FCI) reference energies well within chemical accuracy, achieving an energy error below $3\times10^{-6}$ Ha across 16 geometries with zero variational violations. Mamba-QE maintains high expressive power while establishing a robust, scalable foundation for quantum simulations of complex molecular systems.
items.why: Swaps the Transformer in a generative eigensolver for a Mamba state-space model, tested only on H2.
